subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After authorization ordering is fixed, should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` permanently reject every legacy ownerless session row, or should an explicit migration establish ownership first?
rationale: The ownerless-row behavior changes durable authority and upgrade compatibility; the existing delete rule does not establish whether patch callers should lose access without migration or recovery tooling.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject ownerless rows after fixing write ordering, with a documented operator or non-plugin recovery path.

options.title: Migrate ownership
options.body: Add a narrow doctor or state migration that establishes authority before enforcing the denial.

options.title: Preserve legacy access
options.body: Continue allowing ownerless plugin-runtime patches and explicitly accept the weaker isolation boundary.

recommendation.title: Fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows after fixing write ordering, with a documented operator or non-plugin recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main history signal across the Gateway handler and session projection boundary where this policy must be owned.
